req.title: Session cookie has HttpOnly attribute
req.statement: The system shall set HttpOnly on the session cookie.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that the session cookie carries the HttpOnly attribute. Flask sets the session cookie on any response that writes to the session (e.g. a successful login). We test: (1) positive – after a successful POST /auth/login the Set-Cookie header contains 'HttpOnly'; (2) negative – a plain GET to a non-session-writing endpoint does NOT set a session cookie at all, so there is nothing to check HttpOnly on (verifying the cookie is only emitted when a session is created); (3) boundary – the HttpOnly flag must appear as a distinct token in the Set-Cookie value, not merely as a substring of another attribute name, and the response status must be exactly 302 (redirect after login). Additional tests cover the exact cookie attribute string and confirm the flag is present on the register-then-login flow (STC).

tests.name: test_session_cookie_has_httponly_after_login
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database initialised with fixture data
User 'test' with password 'test' exists in the database
actions: Inspect the Set-Cookie header of the response
expected: Set-Cookie header value contains the token 'HttpOnly' (case-insensitive)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: session cookie must carry HttpOnly attribute
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_session_cookie_has_httponly_after_login():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Expected Set-Cookie header to be present after login'
    assert 'HttpOnly' in set_cookie or 'httponly' in set_cookie.lower(), (
        f'HttpOnly not found in Set-Cookie: {set_cookie}'
    )

tests.name: test_no_session_cookie_on_unauthenticated_get
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
No prior login; session is empty
actions: GET / (blog index) without any prior authentication
expected: No Set-Cookie header is emitted (no session mutation occurred)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly is only relevant when a session cookie is actually set; verifying no spurious cookie is emitted
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_no_session_cookie_on_unauthenticated_get():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    # A plain read-only request must not create a new session cookie
    assert set_cookie == '', (
        f'Unexpected Set-Cookie on unauthenticated GET /: {set_cookie}'
    )

tests.name: test_httponly_is_distinct_token_not_substring
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database initialised with fixture data
User 'test' with password 'test' exists in the database
actions: Split the Set-Cookie header on semicolons
Check each token individually for the exact string 'HttpOnly' (stripped)
expected: At least one semicolon-delimited token in Set-Cookie equals 'HttpOnly' (case-insensitive, stripped)
The token is not merely a prefix or suffix of another attribute name
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly must appear as a standalone attribute token, not embedded in another name
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_httponly_is_distinct_token_not_substring():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header missing after login'
    tokens = [t.strip() for t in set_cookie.split(';')]
    httponly_tokens = [t for t in tokens if t.lower() == 'httponly']
    assert len(httponly_tokens) == 1, (
        f'Expected exactly one HttpOnly token, got {httponly_tokens} in: {set_cookie}'
    )

tests.name: test_session_cookie_httponly_after_register_and_login
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database initialised with fixture data
A new user 'newuser' does not yet exist
actions: Inspect Set-Cookie header of the login response
expected: Set-Cookie header on login response contains 'HttpOnly' token
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly must be set on the session cookie regardless of how the user was created
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_session_cookie_httponly_after_register_and_login():
    r_reg = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'newuser', 'password': 'newpass'})
    assert r_reg.status_code == 302
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'newuser', 'password': 'newpass'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r_login.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header missing after login of newly registered user'
    tokens = [t.strip().lower() for t in set_cookie.split(';')]
    assert 'httponly' in tokens, (
        f'HttpOnly not found as distinct token in Set-Cookie: {set_cookie}'
    )

tests.name: test_failed_login_does_not_set_session_cookie
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database initialised with fixture data
User 'test' exists but wrong password will be supplied
expected: Response status is exactly 200 (re-renders login form with error)
No Set-Cookie header is emitted (no session should be created on failed login)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly cookie must NOT be set when login fails; session is not created
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_failed_login_does_not_set_session_cookie():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'wrongpassword'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    # On failed login no session is written so no session cookie should appear
    assert set_cookie == '', (
        f'Unexpected Set-Cookie on failed login: {set_cookie}'
    )
